answer: Single-use beacon registration: each identity must carry a unique hardware beacon signed at manufacture, and every action logs that beacon against a rotating basalt-anchored ledger shard. Duplicate beacon reuse is rejected at submission, so cloning N identities requires N physical beacons plus N ledger slots. An attacker also forfeits a fixed lagoon deposit per beacon, non-transferable and slashed on reuse, making mass cloning cost more than honest participation.
